summary: This paper proposes a dual metastable-state qubit encoding in $^{171}\mathrm{Yb}$ using the $(6s6p)\,{}^3\mathrm{P}_0$ and $(6s6p)\,{}^3\mathrm{P}_2$ manifolds to enable fast, mid-circuit quantum error correction in neutral-atom arrays. Through full master-equation simulations of gate operations and architectural resource estimation, the authors demonstrate that assigning the ${}^3\mathrm{P}_2$ manifold (with $\Delta_{\mathrm{HF}} = 2\pi \times 6.7$ GHz) to QEC and ${}^3\mathrm{P}_0$ to arithmetic logic reduces circuit overhead while maintaining fault-tolerant capabilities.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction with neutral atoms requires repeated mid-circuit syndrome extraction on ancilla qubits without disturbing data qubits, imposing significant control overhead. A dual-manifold encoding within a single species can exploit distinct coherence and speed properties to separate these functions spectrally rather than spatially.
method: The authors simulate single-qubit gates in ${}^3\mathrm{P}_2$ ($\mathcal{F}_{QB} = 99.916\%$ fidelity, $\Omega = 2\pi \times 2$ MHz), coherent shelving between manifolds via Raman transfer ($\mathcal{F}_{CS} = 99.936\%$), and $\mathcal{CZ}$ gates in Rydberg states, then compile benchmark circuits using a manifold-aware zone-aware compiler to estimate circuit duration and space-time volume for surface-code error correction.
result: For code distances $d \in \{3,5,7\}$, assigning ${}^3\mathrm{P}_2$ to QEC and ${}^3\mathrm{P}_0$ to arithmetic reduces mid-circuit syndrome-extraction overhead and enables parallel execution across blocks; coherence times $T_1 = 1.44$ s and $T_2^* = 82.73$ ms in 850 nm tweezers support hundreds of QEC cycles, with projected logical error rates improving as the ${}^3\mathrm{P}_2$ two-qubit gate error decreases below $0.25\%$.
